title: データベース
subtitle: Database System
educationalGoal: This course mainly deals with relational databases. Its goal is to impart skills in designing databases and in accessing them. Specifically, students are expected to be able to explain relational databases and 3-schema approaches, write queries in SQL, design a database using an entity-relationship diagram, and apply normalization procedures to their database appropriately.
advice: In this course, students will learn the foundations of data models and database management systems focusing on relational databases. There will be report(s) and homework on database design given to check the students' level of understanding. In the curriculum flow, this course is part of the programming and software development track. Therefore, students are expected to pay considerable attention on the mastery of SQL as a programming language.
requiredKnowledge: There is no prerequisite course for Database Systems. Students are required to bring a PC, an AC adapter, and a network cable to the class because there will be exercises where students are asked to write SQL queries and upload them during class hours for later grading.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain what a relational database is.
Be able to explain a 3-schema approach.
Be able to express queries in relational algebra and translate them into SQL.
Be able to design a database using an entity-relationship diagram.
Be able to explain why normalization is necessary and how to do it.
